articles.title: Ethanol imbroglio : Transition must be fuelled by data
articles.description: THE Union government has admitted in Parliament that it has not conducted any assessment to determine the proportion of vehicles in India that are currently compatible with E20 fuel (80 per cent petrol, 20 per cent ethanol). This disclosure reveals a glaring gap between the nation’s green energy ambitions and ground-level preparedness. A nationwide transition can’t be expected to succeed without a comprehensive enumeration. The E20 push is aimed at reducing crude oil imports, cutting emissions and strengthening India’s biofuel economy. The government insists that extensive studies and field trials have found the fuel to be safe for use under prescribed standards. Scientific testing under controlled conditions is valuable, but policymaking affecting millions of motorists requires real-world data.

articles.title: Wall Street's flip from AI to less-loved stocks accelerates, while oil prices keep easing
articles.description: Most U.S. stocks are rising after Coca-Cola and other companies reported stronger profits for the spring than analysts expected. But more drops for chip stocks and other AI winners are keeping Wall Street's gains in check Tuesday, and the S&P 500 rose a relatively modest 0.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 595 points, while the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.1%. The slides for AI stocks were worse elsewhere in the world, and South Korea's Kospi index tumbled nearly 11%. Oil prices continued to ease, which helped to pull Treasury yields lower in the bond market. Brent crude fell toward $82 per barrel.
